titulo: Workshop and B2B community: from free to monthly advisory
lead: The workshop is the cheapest way in and the one that generates the most work afterward: the team learns, the manager sees you in action, and the next conversation is the diagnosis. This lesson shows the 1-hour workshop in 5 parts, the small community of companies, and your plan with dates.
objetivo: design a 1-hour workshop in 5 parts and the ladder from free to monthly advisory, with a dated plan.

aprende.t: Structure the workshop like a flight, in 5 parts
Read the audience and prepare extra content
Build the small community of companies

hero_alt: A facilitator leads a workshop in a meeting room, with about ten people and laptops.

secoes.sub: Parts 1, 2 and 3 fit in the first five minutes.

nos.sub: what they will know how to do
nos.detalhe: Not what you will say: what the person will be able to do afterward. If it doesn't fit in one sentence, the workshop isn't ready.
The map of the journey, acknowledging what the room probably thinks today: "a lot of people here have already tried it and thought it was just a prettier chat".
Announce the technical stretch ahead of time: "around the halfway point there's a boring part, but a quick one, and without it the rest doesn't make sense". Once warned, the room puts up with it.
A shortcut, an example, a number every few minutes. Attention isn't sustained by the promise of a happy ending, but by frequent delivery.
Recap, say how to apply it on Monday, what comes next, and only then open for questions. Ending without a landing leaves the feeling that nothing happened.

secoes.legenda: Teaching is a skill of repetition and feedback, not talent. The structure stands in for talent until it comes.

secoes.sub: Four decisions that change the room.

texto: An analyst wants the detail; the executive team wants the design and the return. Ask the client beforehand who will be in the room.
Required room: open with demos. Voluntary room: they want the fundamentals. Name the fear about jobs in the first few minutes.
If one hour fits 30 slides, prepare 50: most of them are extra examples of the same idea.
Decide beforehand what to skip if the room talks a lot, and keep two backup blocks.
Ask the question and wait. Whoever gives in after three seconds teaches the room not to answer.
If nobody answers, make a light joke and move on. Don't push: your energy doesn't depend on the audience.

exemplo.texto: I can stay quiet for the next few minutes, or you can give me a hint so I can adapt the examples to your work.

texto: Whoever uses examples from one industry attracts clients from that industry. Use the real vocabulary: enrollment, policy, appraisal report, deed.
If the clients who show up are from the wrong industry, look at your examples.

secoes.titulo: The small community and the access ladder
secoes.sub: Seven to ten companies, not seven hundred people. Ranges are orders of magnitude: adapt to your market.

texto: Basic templates, a monthly bulletin with what changed, questions answered in public, and the open office hours.
It needs to be good enough for someone to recommend it without ever having paid.

passos.sub: good enough to pay for every month
texto: Advanced guides, real cases, long sessions with live building, members-only office hours.
A group of companies usually lands in the US$ 100 to 500 per company per month range. With 7 to 10, you know each one's problem.
A defined response window, with rules, not unlimited access to your life.
Whoever moves up has already proven, on the previous step, that they extract value.
After the call: "instead of filling your inbox, I have a space where I answer questions like the ones we discussed".
After the workshop: "if you want to bring your own company's case, this is the space".

secoes.sub: The 1-hour script with the minutes in view.

blocos.conteudo:
WORKSHOP · <topic> · <company> · <date>
Audience: <roles> · mandatory or voluntary: <which>
Destination (1 sentence): after this hour, you will be able to <do what>.

00-05 OPENING
- Hook: <image or demo running>
- So what: <what changes for those who pay attention>
- Path and flight plan: <warn about the technical stretch>
- Name the fear: <sentence>

05-20 MODULE 1 · foundation (light, lots of examples)
- Concept → when to use → before and after → example from the industry
- Question for the room (wait 15 s): <question>

20-40 MODULE 2 · the densest (at peak attention)
- <technical content warned about in the flight plan>
- Question for the room: <question>

40-55 MODULE 3 · applied (attention has already dropped)
- Day-to-day example: <what changes tomorrow morning>
- Vision example: <what changes in 12 months>

55-60 LANDING
- Recap 3 points · how to apply on Monday · what comes next
- Questions · invitation: <community or office hours>

BACKUP (if the room goes quiet): <block A>, <block B>
SKIP (if the room talks a lot): <block>

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: The room was forced to attend your workshop. How do you open?
opcoes: With the fundamentals, to get everyone on the same level
With demos, to earn their attention before you teach
By asking each person to introduce themselves
perguntas.explica: A mandatory audience arrives with arms crossed: you earn their attention first. Fundamentals first is for a room that came by choice.

perguntas.p: You asked a question and the room went silent. What do you do?
opcoes: Answer it yourself after three seconds
Wait about fifteen seconds; if no one speaks, move on without pushing
Ask for participation again, with more emphasis
perguntas.explica: If you give in fast, you teach the room not to answer; if you push, it gets awkward. Wait, use the line that breaks the ice, and move on.

perguntas.p: Where do you put the most technical part of the workshop?
opcoes: At the end, for the people who stayed
In the middle, at the attention peak, announced in the flight plan
At the beginning, to get it over with
perguntas.explica: Attention rises after the opening and drops at the end. The dense block goes in the middle and is announced beforehand, so the room can stay with you.

perguntas.p: Why a community of 7 to 10 companies, and not hundreds of people?
opcoes: Because it is easier to promote
Because you know each one's problem and notice the loss of interest before the cancellation
Because companies will pay any amount
perguntas.explica: With a few companies you really talk, and you see the silence that comes before a cancellation. A company approves a monthly fee as an expense and doesn't cancel just because the month got tight.

itens.texto: Destination, route, and flight plan fit in the first five minutes.
Mandatory or voluntary changes the opening; extra examples save a silent room.
Fifteen seconds of waiting, and the vocabulary of the people you want to serve.
Free is good for referrals, paid is good for revenue, monthly advisory sits at the top.
